newsitem.title: UK: Protest planned against Northern Ireland march.
newsitem.headline: Protest planned against Northern Ireland march.

text.p: Roman Catholic activists said on Thursday that they would hold a protest march during a Protestant parade on Saturday, reviving memories of sectarian tensions fired by Northern Ireland parades in July.

The Bogside Residents Association said in a statement that the planned parade by the Apprentice Boys around the walls of Londonderry was confrontation and called for a counter-march at the same location.
Spokesman Donncha MacNiallais said 13 people from Londonderry's Catholic Bogside area would walk along the walls at exactly the same time as 200 members of the Apprentice Boys.
He denied that they would try to block the parade. "I don't think you could say that 13 people protesting could be described as an attempt to block the parade," he said.

Police have not yet decided whether to allow the Apprentice Boys, one of several Protestant-based organisations which celebrate their roots in Northern Ireland by staging annual marches, to hold the parade.
MacNiallais said the "arrogant" refusal of the Apprentice Boys to negotiate over the parade was "triumphalism, coat-trailing and confrontational."
"Our community expects equality and paritiy of esteem. We are determined to ensure that these rights are accorded to us," he said.
The row over the parade awakened fears of renewed sectarian tension in an atmosphere charged by an Irish Republican Army (IRA) bomb attack on Britain's army headquarters in the province last week.

The Londonderry parade was postponed in July when violence swept the province over a march by the Orange Order through the mainly Catholic area of the southern town of Portadown. Catholics regard the parades as intimidation and triumphalism.
Protestant protests forced police to reverse a ban on the Portadown march. It went ahead, sparking a wave of Catholic protests which led to the banning of the Londonderry march.

Spokesmen for the Apprentice Boys were not immediately available for comment on the Bogside statement, but members have said they do not see any need for talks with Bogside residents and always planned to hold the parade.

The original march was prevented by security forces who blocked off the walls with concrete and iron fences to prevent the Apprentice Boys marching along a section which directly overlooks the Bogside.
The Apprentice Boys take their name from 13 trainee workers who slammed shut the gates of the city in the 17th century to prevent King James 11, a Catholic monarch, taking the city.
